title: Polymorphism
points: The same method call behaves differently depending on the actual object type.
The caller uses the parent type or interface; the behaviour is picked at runtime (overriding, dynamic dispatch).
trade: Runtime polymorphism = overriding. Compile-time = overloading. A chain of instanceof or switch on type is the smell that polymorphism is missing.
test: CheckoutService.checkout(PaymentMethod m, double total) calls m.pay(total), where PaymentMethod is an interface implemented by StripePayment and PayPalPayment. How does polymorphism let you add a GrabPayPayment without changing CheckoutService?
answer: The service calls pay() on the interface. A new payment type is a new class implementing it, and the right pay() runs at runtime.
